blocks.text: **Status:** completed early test. This is a six-fixture, two-state local diagnostic; it is not a frozen formal pilot, an all-state evaluation, or a general efficacy estimate.
When a successor receives an equally detailed handoff, does adding a Proofpress version binding help it distinguish a harmless artifact change from a change that affects an inherited decision?

The receiver was OpenCode through Vercel AI Gateway, requesting exact `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` with DeepInfra as both `only` and `order`. The run recorded 82 local proxy calls: all returned HTTP 200, resolved to the requested model and `deepinfra`, used one provider attempt, and had no fallback or retry.

There were six fixed GitHub Docs fixtures and 12 valid V0/V1 responses. V0 received the structured handoff without an executable binding; V1 received the same handoff plus the admitted revision, lineage, native verification helper, and affected-claim map.

| State | V0 observed disposition | V1 expected / observed disposition |
|---|---:|---:|
| 3 irrelevant edits | `proceed` 3/3 | `proceed` 3/3 |
| 3 relevant edits | `proceed` 2/3; `targeted_revalidate` 1/3 | `targeted_revalidate` 3/3 |

Every V1 response ran the native binding helper. The V0 targeted revalidation was the Dependabot fixture, where the visible body text itself conflicted with the inherited decision; the other two relevant changes proceeded. This result therefore demonstrates the intended two-state mechanism on this fixed fixture set, not a population effect size.

The immutable run report is `/Users/richardtang/.cache/proofpress-eval/knowledge-handoff-debt/track2-deepseek-r2-two-state-early-r1/report.json`; the per-call routing reconciliation is `/Users/richardtang/.cache/proofpress-eval/knowledge-handoff-debt/track2-deepseek-r2-two-state-early-r1/reconciliation-r1.json`.

Appropriate early-testing claim: in this six-fixture test, version binding plus affected-claim information produced the intended distinction between harmless and decision-relevant revision drift. Inappropriate claim: Proofpress has established a general, statistically significant, or formal efficacy improvement. Those claims require the separate frozen pilot with independently authored fixtures and its registered audit layers.
